To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

D1 and D4 dopamine receptor and m4 muscari nic acetylcholine receptors were localized in the striatonigral projection neurons, whereas D2 dopamine receptors were localized in striatopallidal projection neurons.
D1 and D4 receptor immunoreactivities colocalized with striatonigral neuron somata, but D2 and m4 receptor protein immunoreactivities did not.

D1 and D4 receptor proteins were colocalized to a large majority of rat neostriatal neurons, whereas D2 receptor proteins were colocolized with D1 or D4 receptor proteins in a small minority of these neurons.

the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of dopamine and acetycholine on the activity of the basal ganglia.
how the basal ganglia, a group of subcortical structures, control movement.
how the brain processes information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D1 and D4 receptor immunoreactivities are present in 95% of striatonigral projection neurons.
D1 and D4 receptors are localized in striatonigral (GPe‐ and STN‐projecting) neurons, whereas D2 receptors are localized in the striatopallidal (GPi‐ and SNr‐projecting) neuron population.
D1 receptors are localized to the majority of striatonigral projection neurons, while m4 receptors are localized to a subset of these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D1 receptor expression is a marker for striatonigral cells and that m4 receptor expression is a co‐marker with D1 receptor expression for striatonigraal cells.
the D1 receptor is expressed in all striatonigral projection neurons and that the D2 receptor is not expressed at all in these projection neurons.
D1 receptors are expressed in all striatonigral (SNr) neurons and m4 receptors in most of these neurons, while D2 receptors are not expressed in these neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the two major classes of dopamine receptors (D1 and D2) are expressed in distinct populations of striatal neurons, and that the two major subtypes of muscarinic acetycholine receptors (m1 and m4) are expressed in the same populations of striatal projection cells.
the D1 and m2 receptors are colocalized in striatal projection neurons.
dopamine receptor proteins are differentially distributed in the striatum.
